paragraphs: A firm that moved its staff to a four-day week reported that productivity did not decline over the following six months. Supporters cite this as evidence that long workweeks are largely wasted time. A more cautious reading would note that employees knew they were being observed and had every reason to protect a perk they valued. It would also note that the firm's work is unusually self-paced, so that its result may not extend to a call center or a hospital ward, where output depends on being present. The trial is nonetheless valuable, because it shows that in at least one setting the long week was not necessary.
